name: AI Shorts Review And Refine
use_when: A long-form podcast, interview, livestream, or talking-head video needs short-form repurposing.
An AI clipping tool has generated candidate shorts, reframes, captions, or layouts.
The agent needs to accelerate selection without trusting automatic output blindly.
avoid_when: The original footage has sensitive context that could be misleading when clipped.
The short cannot make sense without setup that would exceed the platform duration.
The user requires manual editorial judgment for every beat and does not want automated candidates.

timeline_pattern.pattern: generate_candidates -> watch_candidates -> select_self_contained_clip -> trim_start_end -> choose_layout -> fix_captions -> context_text -> export_or_schedule
timeline_pattern.selection_rule: Only keep clips with a clear premise, tension, useful point, and payoff when viewed independently.
timeline_pattern.trim_rule: Adjust AI start and end points so the clip does not begin mid-thought or end before the payoff.
timeline_pattern.layout_rule: Choose fill, fit, split, or multi-speaker layouts based on who is speaking and what visual context matters.

motion.rule: Auto-reframing must keep the active speaker, reactions, and proof visuals visible; reject layouts that overwhelm the frame.

sound.rule: Do not cut audio so tightly that the speech sounds chopped; preserve tiny natural lead-in/out when needed.

captions.rule: Review every caption. Remove filler-word captions or bad emphasis without cutting meaningful audio.
captions.layout_rule: Captions should not cover faces, titles, cards, or the visual reason the clip was chosen.

color.rule: Maintain a consistent look between long-form source and short-form crop; avoid auto-templates that hide faces or products.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use crop/scale/pad for 9:16 versions, burn corrected captions after layout review, and render short candidate previews before final batching.
implementation.remotion: Represent AI candidates as data with sourceStart, sourceEnd, score, layout, captionEdits, contextText, and approved fields.
implementation.blender: Use only for custom animated context cards or branded interstitials when needed.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use auto-captions and templates as a first pass, then manually trim, reframe, edit captions, and remove weak layouts.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use sequence auto-reframe and captions as drafts, then manually adjust crop, speaker framing, caption breaks, and exports.

common_mistakes: Publishing AI-selected clips without checking whether the clip works alone.
Accepting an auto-start that cuts off the premise.
Leaving captions on filler words that make the short feel messy.
Using a multi-person layout that shrinks the actual speaker or proof too much.
Creating a misleading claim by removing surrounding context.
qc: Does the clip make sense without the original long-form video?
Does the first second contain a clear premise, tension, or useful point?
Are start and end trims natural and complete?
Are captions accurate, readable, and free of distracting filler emphasis?
Does the layout keep speaker faces, reactions, and proof visible?
Could the clip misrepresent the original context?
